label: Induction cooktop

questions.text: How long is it used each day?
questions.why: Long cooking heats the electronics inside.

questions.text: What cookware is used on it?
questions.why: Only induction-ready cookware works well; the wrong kind can damage it.

questions.text: Does the power at home often dip, flicker or trip?
questions.why: Unsteady power can damage the electronics.

questions.text: Are the air vents kept clear?
Do spills often reach the vents or the control panel?
Have you noticed error codes, cracks on the glass or it switching off by itself?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the cooktop, and let the glass cool, before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: The surface stays hot and cleaning it while powered risks a shock.

care_tips.text: Don't open the cooktop yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.

care_tips.text: Stop using it if the glass is cracked, and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: Cracked glass can let liquid reach live parts.

care_tips.text: Use induction-ready cookware with a flat base.
care_tips.why: The wrong cookware heats poorly and can trigger errors.

care_tips.text: Use a surge protector or stabilizer if the power is unsteady.
care_tips.why: Power swings can damage the board.

care_tips.text: Wipe spills once the glass has cooled.
care_tips.why: Burnt spills are harder to clean and can stain.

reminders.text: Check the cooktop's air vents are clean (unplugged and cool).
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
